# 3Dviz Pro Max — shared skill adapter

Upstream: https://github.com/viettranx/3dviz-pro-max (MIT).
Pinned revision: `d077e0e68915c25be8e71d74684d3144fd1c2aca`.

## Locate full resources before using them

1. If `.ai-tools/3dviz-pro-max/skill/SKILL.md` exists, use that project's full pre-existing installation and its adjacent resources.
2. Otherwise use `.ai-tools/upstream/3dviz-pro-max/skills/3dviz-pro-max/SKILL.md`. If absent, the pinned Git submodule has not been checked out. From project root, if allowed: `git submodule update --init .ai-tools/upstream/3dviz-pro-max`.
3. Read the selected original `SKILL.md` **before** starting specialized work. Resolve all referenced scripts, data, templates and kits relative to its actual directory, not this adapter. Consult its license and supporting docs.
4. If full resources are unavailable, continue with existing project tools and state that the full upstream skill was not loaded; do not claim its catalogs, scripts or checks were used.

Use for 3D, 2.5D, spatial interaction, perspective, models, environments and materials **when relevant**. Detect and preserve the project's actual engine, visual direction, controls and artistic constraints. Pair with CodeGraph for code paths, Spec Kit for plans, Superpowers for implementation/QA, gamedev-router for game-specific workflows and Obscura for web rendering if installed. Do not add Three.js, Blender or other dependencies without an actual need. Verify the rendered scene and interactions: a build or script passing is not visual proof.

# Game-dev skills router — shared adapter

Upstream: https://github.com/gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills (Apache-2.0).
Pinned revision: `19d93f97c9c1ea0f8b306e77aa81e0d3e352d3e9`.

## Read the source of truth

- Prefer an already-installed `.agents/skills/router/SKILL.md` if this project includes its own curated game-dev suite (for example, The Horde); do not replace that suite.
- Otherwise read `.ai-tools/upstream/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills/router/SKILL.md` and its references, from the pinned submodule. If absent and permitted, run from project root: `git submodule update --init .ai-tools/upstream/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills`.
- After reading the router, select only the relevant original `SKILL.md` files under the upstream `skills/` hierarchy. Do not guess names or load every skill. Resolve their references from their real folders.
- If the full source isn't installed or accessible, this adapter offers only routing guidance; do not claim the full library was loaded.

## Route only when the task concerns games

1. Identify the *actual* engine (e.g., Godot, Unity, Unreal, Phaser, PixiJS, three.js, Canvas/DOM custom engine) from project files; don't impose an engine because a vendor folder exists.
2. Pick the smallest relevant discipline: gameplay/AI, game feel, physics/input, level design, performance, UI/UX, sprites/assets/VFX, audio, saves, online or testing. Add a genre guide only when relevant.
3. Preserve the current engine, source-of-truth gameplay files, lore, visual proportions, existing plans and saved-game schemas. Apply project-specific skills and instructions first.
4. Use CodeGraph to map dependencies, Spec Kit to specify substantial changes, Superpowers for debugging/tests and 3Dviz when spatial design matters. Verify assets *in-game*, not just by listing/generated filenames.

For non-game repositories, ignore this skill unless developing a genuine game component or interactive simulation.

# Spec Kit — shared readiness router

Source: https://github.com/github/spec-kit (MIT). This adapter complements—not replaces—any real `speckit-*` skills, official CLI or existing `.specify/` installation.

1. Read `AGENTS.md` and `.ai-tools/README.md` (if present) for the project's verified Spec Kit integration and revisions. Look for `.specify/`, `.agents/skills/speckit-*/SKILL.md`, `.claude/commands/` and existing specs, plans and tasks.
2. When corresponding project skills and `.specify/` exist, use the actual `speckit-specify`, `speckit-plan`, `speckit-tasks` and `speckit-implement` workflows in order **only as needed**. Do not substitute this router for their complete commands or run commands unavailable in the current client.
3. If not installed, first use `python3 .ai-tools/setup.py doctor` only where that script exists. Follow the project's documented Spec Kit preparation/review procedure rather than writing an incomplete `.specify/` or claiming installation.
4. Reuse and update existing work instead of duplicating specifications. Respect project conventions, scope and past decisions. For small fixes, follow the existing development workflow without forcing a lengthy spec process.
5. Combine with CodeGraph for dependency context, Superpowers for design/debug/QA and other domain skills where relevant; builds and tests remain required.

No command package, plugin or runtime is installed by this text file alone.

Read [the shared Spec Kit router](../../../.agents/skills/speckit-router/SKILL.md) and the existing project setup guide `.ai-tools/README.md` when available. Check actual `.specify/` and commands before invoking them. Avoid re-initializing an existing project or claiming official commands are installed when they are not.

# Shared AI skills — pinned opt-in integration

This repository keeps its existing skills, prompts, AGENTS.md and build conventions. Additional reusable adapters are exposed for **Codex** (`.agents/skills/`) and **Claude Code** (`.claude/skills/`).

| Skill | Where to start | Canonical upstream | Local availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3Dviz Pro Max | `.agents/skills/3dviz-pro-max/SKILL.md` | [viettranx/3dviz-pro-max](https://github.com/viettranx/3dviz-pro-max) (MIT, `d077e0e68915c25be8e71d74684d3144fd1c2aca`) | Use the existing `.ai-tools/3dviz-pro-max/skill/` install or the pinned Git submodule |
| Game-dev router | `.agents/skills/gamedev-router/SKILL.md` | [gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills](https://github.com/gamedev-skills/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills) (Apache-2.0, `19d93f97c9c1ea0f8b306e77aa81e0d3e352d3e9`) | Prefer local project game-dev skills; otherwise pinned Git submodule |
| Spec Kit readiness | `.agents/skills/speckit-router/SKILL.md` | [github/spec-kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) (MIT) | Follow the project's existing `.ai-tools/README.md` and real `.specify/` setup |

To fetch the **two full external skill catalogs** after cloning (the remote packages are *not* vendored into this repository's Git history):

```sh
git submodule update --init .ai-tools/upstream/3dviz-pro-max .ai-tools/upstream/awesome-gamedev-agent-skills
```

Check that their `SKILL.md` files exist at the paths described in each adapter before using them. These submodules are pinned to immutable commits, do not run on CI merely by being declared and should not be upgraded silently. If the Git client did not fetch submodules, the adapters remain discoverable but the **full upstream library is not available**. Never claim it was loaded without reading the files.

The project-local packages (Obscura and any game-specific, 3Dviz, Spec Kit, CCGS or CodeGraph tools) are retained. Git submodules and skill descriptions alone do not install MCP servers, IDE plugins or build dependencies. Route tasks according to relevance; non-game projects are not obliged to use game-development guidance.
